deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss is continuing a reduction of the French triangulation by the ingénieur-géographe Epailly ("Epaillysche Dreiecke"). The chain starts from the side Bentheim–Kirchhesepe (Kirchhesepe is probably Groß Hesepe in the Emsland) and runs through Uelsen (written Ulsen), Coevorden, Lemelerberg, Beilen, Sleen, Rolde and Onstwedde. The next page carries it on via Groningen, Midwolde, Leer, Emden, Aurich, Strackholt and Westerstede into East Frisia. This was presumably done to tie the Dutch–East-Frisian triangles to his own Hanoverian network.

Table layout: for each station P, the stations Q sighted from it are listed. The columns are:
(1) a raw direction (azimuth) T_PQ in degrees, minutes and seconds;
(2) a correction c_PQ in arcseconds;
(3) the reduced direction t_PQ = T_PQ + c_PQ;
(4) log10 of the side length s_PQ, in metres. For example 10^4.4841439 ≈ 30 497 m for Bentheim–Uelsen, which fits the real geography.

The directions are reckoned from south through west, as Gauss usually does. On that reading, Bentheim→Kirchhesepe = 190°43′ means about 10° east of north, and Kirchhesepe→Uelsen = 65° means west-southwest. Both fit the map.

What the reduction achieves (inferred, checked numerically below):
(a) After correction, reciprocal directions differ by exactly 180°: t_QP = t_PQ ± 180°. The pairs are Bentheim–Uelsen 142°27′37.526″/322°27′37.526″, Bentheim–Kirchhesepe 190°43′38.235″/10°43′38.235″, Kirchhesepe–Uelsen 65°34′34.660″/245°34′34.660″, Kirchhesepe–Coevorden 99°3′39.017″/279°3′39.017″, and Uelsen–Coevorden 154°18′13.188″/334°18′13.188″.
(b) Before correction, the reciprocal pairs miss 180° by +24.396″, −33.712″, −11.407″, +5.405″ and +18.127″ respectively. In each case the two end corrections sum exactly to minus that misclosure. Examples: 12.009 + 12.387 = 24.396; 16.958 + 16.754 = 33.712; 5.581 + 5.826 = 11.407; 2.627 + 2.778 = 5.405; 9.006 + 9.121 = 18.127.
(c) The misclosure is split almost, but not exactly, in half. The asymmetries are 0.19″, 0.10″, 0.12″, 0.08″ and 0.06″. So the corrections are computed reductions (arc-to-chord type), not a mechanical halving.
(d) In triangle Bentheim–Kirchhesepe–Uelsen the raw angles are 48°15′55.760″ + 54°50′45.252″ + 76°53′21.079″ = 180°0′2.091″. The excess of 2.091″ matches the spherical excess. My estimate: area ≈ ½·30497·36325·sin48.27° m² ≈ 4.13·10^8 m², giving ε ≈ area/R²·ρ ≈ 2.09″.
(e) The corrected angles are 48°16′0.709″ + 54°50′56.425″ + 76°53′2.866″ = 180°0′0.000″ exactly. Triangle Kirchhesepe–Uelsen–Coevorden likewise closes to exactly 180° after reduction: 33°29′4.357″ + 91°16′21.472″ + 55°14′34.171″.
(f) The log sides satisfy the plane law of sines with the reduced angles. For example, log(BK) − log(BU) = 0.0759594 ≈ log(sin76°53′2.866″ / sin54°50′56.425″).

Interpretation (mine, hedged): the raw values are spheroidal directions referred to a common orientation, not to each station's own meridian. The corrections reduce them to bearings of straight chords in a plane (conformal) projection. Their size, up to about 17″ on 30–36 km lines, is consistent with Gauss's conformal projection about a distant central meridian such as Göttingen's. Every addition and subtraction on the page is exact. The remaining stations (Lemelerberg, Beilen, Sleen, Rolde, Onstwedde, with Sleen struck out under Beilen) are listed as a skeleton without values, waiting to be filled in.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: all ten sums T + c = t are exact to 0.001″, reciprocal reduced directions differ by exactly 180°, and both reduced triangles close to 180°0′0.000″.
Not an error but incomplete: rows for Lemelerberg, Beilen, Sleen, Rolde and Onstwedde are blank; only five lines are reduced.

results.what: Reduction of spheroidal/spherical triangulation directions to plane chord bearings, so that reciprocal bearings differ by 180° and triangles close to 180° (spherical excess removed by direction corrections)
results.modern_name: Direction (arc-to-chord, t−T) reduction for a conformal map projection (Gauss conformal / Gauss–Krüger)
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (Hanover survey, 1820s); later systematized by Schreiber and Krüger

results.what: Re-reduction of Epailly's French triangle chain Bentheim–Kirchhesepe–Uelsen–Coevorden toward East Frisia, presumably to link with Gauss's Hanoverian triangulation
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's Hanover arc measurement and land survey (connection to Krayenhoff/Epailly data)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine computational work for Gauss's geodetic survey: a tabulated reduction of Epailly's directions to plane bearings, using his well-known conformal-projection technique. It is worth noting as a documentary trace of the use of Epailly's triangles, but it contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Raw reciprocal misclosure on Bentheim–Uelsen (24.396″) equals sum of the two end corrections
Reduced triangle Bentheim–Kirchhesepe–Uelsen closes exactly to 180°
Raw angle sum excess = 2.091″ (spherical excess of the triangle)
Reduced triangle Kirchhesepe–Uelsen–Coevorden closes exactly to 180°
Plane law of sines: log BK − log BU = log(sin U / sin K), ≈ 0 to ~1e-6
Plane law of sines: log KU − log BU = log(sin B / sin K), ≈ 0
Spherical excess estimate ≈ 2.09″, matching the raw misclosure

transcription_corrections: Station names as written vs. modern: 'Ulsen' = Uelsen, 'Coeverden' = Coevorden, 'Kirchhesepe' = (Groß) Hesepe, 'Gröningen' (next page) = Groningen.
Under 'Beilen' the entry 'Sleen' is heavily struck through (correctly marked [-Sleen-]).
Transcription values agree with the image; the 6th digit in '142.27.37,526' and the '1' in '4.4841439' are overwritten but read as given.
The title reads 'von der Seite' (possibly abbreviated 'Seite' with a flourish).
